reason: The text explicitly portrays the Hebrew people (עָם) in direct relationship with Yahweh (יְהוָה), who speaks to Moses and gives them commandments (מִצְוֺתַי) and Torah (תוֹרֹתָֽי). The passage narrates the people receiving divine instruction regarding manna and the Sabbath, and they obey these commands (וַיִּשְׁבְּת֥וּ הָעָ֖ם - 'the people rested on the seventh day'). The text explicitly identifies Yahweh as their God and demonstrates their adherence to His directives, establishing them clearly as followers of the God Yahweh.
